plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, paying only that amount, and you never risk overpaying since payment is based on the second-highest bid, not your own. Since this is a single-round game with independent draws, there's no need to shade my bid for future strategic reasons. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $23 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values. In such auctions, bidding truthfully (bidding exactly my value) is a weakly dominant strategy, regardless of what other bidders do. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding my true value maximizes my expected profit - I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid, and pay less than my value when I do win. There's no strategic advantage to bidding above or below my true value of $18.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors. This holds because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so there's no incentive to shade your bid up or down—overbidding risks losing money if you win, and underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With my value at $39, I should bid exactly $39 to maximize expected profit.
